native_result.query: In what centuries did we see the highest growth phase of the period between 2000 BCE and 1100 BCE?
native_result.HypoA: Between 1500 BCE and 1300 BCE, highest growth of the period between 2000 BCE and 1100 BCE is seen.
native_result.HypoB: The highest-growth phase of 2000-1100 BCE was the 15th-14th centuries BCE (1500-1401 BCE): the peak demographic/openness growth rate (pollen_grate_100) and KDE growth rate (g_all_mean) both occur in the 15th century BCE (1500-1401), immediately followed by the strongest capital expansion in the 14th century BCE (1400-1301), led by Social capital (Delta +1.53) and Economic capital. Growth then declines through the 13th century and is clearly negative in the 12th century BCE (1200-1101 BCE), the weakest period in the window on all signals.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded time_series_data.csv, capital.csv (comma decimals) and the Belau/Woserin pollen openness file; restricted to 2000-1100 BCE inclusive (901 annual rows, zero missing values in kde_all_mean, g_all_mean, pollen_inter_100, pollen_grate_100); binned annual data onto the capital.csv century grid (bin BCE=X covers X..X-99; CE=-1100 endpoint isolated); computed century means of pollen_grate_100 (primary growth signal) and g_all_mean (corroborating KDE growth); built four documented capital category indices (Symbolic, Social, Cultural, Economic) and pooled AllCapital from within-category means of the 12 Z columns and computed century-on-century deltas Z(X)-Z(X+100); ranked all 9 centuries by each signal; sensitivity check via pct-change and absolute level change of SMOOTH_MEAN_100y from the raw pollen file (time-ascending; zero-crossing artifact in the 1600 BCE bin identified and excluded from interpretation).
